generation.prompt_exact:
Create a production sprite sheet of FOUR distinct Southern California native woody plants for ChirpNeighbors. Actual detailed naturalistic PIXEL ART with small crisp square pixel clusters and carefully stepped edges; restrained rich organic shading, subtle dark contour selectively, warm upper-left light, slight top visibility with three-quarter side garden view. This should be fine detailed premium environmental game art, not cartoons, chibi, low-detail icons, painterly blur, glossy 3D, or UI. These quiet plants support birds as scene focus; no birds or animals in this image.

Exactly four isolated full plant sprites arranged in a generous 2 by 2 grid on TRUE transparent alpha background, ideally 2048 by 2048 pixels. Keep all branches completely within each separate quadrant with wide empty gutters and padding. No labels, text, borders, pots, plaques, panels, ground rectangles, checkerboard or decorative backdrop. Each plant stands at the bottom center of its own quadrant with a visible natural root collar and only a few tiny contact pebbles, no large baked shadow. Match coherent camera/light. Composition uses canvas efficiently but do not let plants touch; each tree or shrub can be represented at its own fit-to-cell scale, these are not physical size comparisons.

UPPER LEFT: California sycamore (Platanus racemosa), healthy green leaf state, a small mature specimen with spreading irregular forked limbs, broad deeply lobed fresh green leaves, distinctive mottled cream gray and warm tan trunk, visually readable pale trunks showing through layered foliage. Clearly deciduous broadleaf morphology, not an oak.
UPPER RIGHT: Torrey pine (Pinus torreyana), coastal wind-shaped open asymmetrical spreading crown, long blue-green needle tufts clustered at branch tips, rugged thick furrowed brown trunk, a few small stout cones; distinct from a Christmas fir or generic conical pine. Healthy evergreen state.
LOWER LEFT: Sugar bush (Rhus ovata), dense rounded large shrub with visible reddish young branch forks, broad leathery oval olive green leaves characteristically folded along midrib; subtle tiny pale spring clusters only as accent. It must read as broadleaf chaparral shrub, not fern or bush flowers.
LOWER RIGHT: Mainland hollyleaf cherry (Prunus ilicifolia subsp. ilicifolia), irregular multistem small tree/shrub with glossy deep green hollylike sharply toothed leaves and a few understated creamy-white upright flower racemes; distinct branching silhouette and leaf texture from sugar bush, not a holiday holly or red-berry toyon.

Deliver actual clean transparent sprites with detailed botanical structure, separate silhouettes, no caption. Crisp pixel art, not photographs. This is one flattened sheet of four separately extractable whole sprites, not independently layered trunks and foliage.
